archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical revival)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old rhythm thrower who wins from a clean pocket by avoiding sacks and, this season, by pushing the ball downfield more than he has in years, with his tight ends and Tre Tucker as his main reads.

report.headline: Deep-ball resurgence is real; the accuracy slide and the TD rate aren't safe
report.take:
Cousins came to Las Vegas off the weakest season of his prime: in 2025 he posted 6.4 yards an attempt, a -2.8 CPOE that ranked 45th, and 191 yards a game. Seven starts in, he has 16 touchdowns (first among 45 qualifiers), 268 yards a game (6th) and 0.144 EPA per dropback (15th), up 0.104 on the league average. His yards per attempt is up 0.9 on last year and his aggressiveness has climbed to 20.6%, the highest of any season on his record. Raiders coaches have taken the leash off, and he has answered with a downfield game that looks nothing like the checkdown version from Atlanta.

The value is concentrated in a few places. His 27 throws of 20+ air yards have produced 0.861 EPA a play with a +9.2 CPOE, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Throws of 10+ yards account for nearly all of his passing EPA, while everything under 10 yards adds almost nothing, and the screens and throws behind the line are a real drain at -11 EPA. Bowers and Tucker each return 0.46 EPA a target, while Jeanty's 45 targets barely clear zero. He's also keeping drives alive with his pocket management: a 3.7% sack rate (6th) and a 14.8% pressure-to-sack rate (3rd). That fits his career, since he has always taken fewer sacks than his pressure would predict.

The box score flatters him in two ways. First, the volume comes from circumstances: the run game ranks 31st in EPA and the defense 22nd, dead last against short passes. So Las Vegas throws, often from behind, and the last five games average 39.6 attempts and 292.8 yards. Second, the accuracy is slipping. The play-by-play CPOE is -1.16 (31st), the intermediate window has produced four of his five interceptions on a 49.2% completion rate, and over the last three games his CPOE is 4.6 points below his season mark. That stretch included -9.7 against Buffalo and -7.9 against the Rams. His red-zone line, 12 touchdowns with no picks, sits on a 33% success rate, which looks more like a hot run of finishing than a repeatable rate.

Where it's heading: the arm talent on deep throws and the sack avoidance are sustainable, and the pass-heavy script isn't going away with this run game and defense. Expect the yards to hold. Expect the touchdowns to drift toward a normal rate, and more interceptions over the middle if the CPOE trend keeps sliding at 38. He's a strong volume passer on a losing team, not the top-five efficiency QB the touchdown column suggests.

strengths.title: Downfield throws carry the offense
strengths.body: Throws of 20+ air yards return 0.861 EPA a play with a +9.2 CPOE and no interceptions. Throws of 10+ yards produce nearly all of his passing value. Twenty-seven attempts is a small sample, so the efficiency will cool. Still, a career-high aggressiveness rate shows the coaches are calling these on purpose.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance keeps drives alive
strengths.body: He's pressured on about a fifth of dropbacks, a middling rate, but turns only 14.8% of those pressures into sacks, third-best in the league. His overall sack rate sits three points under the league average. His career pressure-to-sack ranks show this is a long-standing trait, not luck, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Two tight ends plus Tucker
strengths.body: Bowers and Tucker each return 0.46 EPA a target on heavy volume, and Mayer adds 0.263 as a third reliable option. That trio covers for a run game that gives him nothing. Their target volume is the most sustainable part of his profile.

concerns.title: Accuracy sliding, especially over the middle
concerns.body: His play-by-play CPOE ranks 31st and has dropped sharply over the last three games. The intermediate window (49.2% completions, -6.9 CPOE, four interceptions) and the middle of the field (-9.9 CPOE) are where it shows. With CPOE also negative in 2025, this looks like age-related decline rather than noise. It's the main thing that could turn his aggressiveness into turnovers.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate due to regress
concerns.body: A 6.2% TD rate sits 1.7 points above the league average. Twelve red-zone scores on a 33% success rate points to finishing luck as much as skill. His recent TD rate has already dropped below his season mark, so expect fewer than the 39-TD pace.

concerns.title: Volume is a product of losing
concerns.body: The 31st-ranked run game and a defense that's 22nd in EPA keep Las Vegas throwing from behind. That inflates his yards during a 1-4 stretch. The volume should last, but it reflects the team's flaws more than his own efficiency. The screen game is a dead spot that doesn't help either.

trend.note: Yardage and attempts have climbed during the 0-3 skid, and efficiency over the last five is slightly above his season mark. But his completion accuracy has fallen hard in Weeks 6-7, and the Rams game was his only negative-EPA outing.

nextGame.headline: Soft Jets pass defense, but it limits yardage and gets home
nextGame.body:
The Jets fit his game well in some ways. They're 7th in EPA against the run, so Las Vegas' bad ground game will be even less viable. Against the pass they rank 25th, and they're 27th against short throws. The counterweights are real, though. They hold quarterbacks to the 5th-fewest yards a game and keep opposing WR1s 5.1 PPR points under their averages, which matters for Tucker. Their 5th-ranked sack rate tests his pocket management, which is his strongest skill.

Availability tilts slightly his way. The Jets are without edge Joseph Ossai and may lack DT T'Vondre Sweat, two rotational linemen who play close to half the snaps. On their offense, Breece Hall and guard Dylan Parham are out, which could slow the Jets down and keep this nearer to a coin-flip game, as the Book's 1.5-point line suggests. For Cousins, a close game may mean fewer of the trailing-script attempts that have padded his yardage. Jack Bech has been designated to return, but his part-time role barely moves the passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Bowers against a middling TE defense
keyMatchups.body: The Jets rank mid-pack against top tight ends and let TE1s roughly match their usual output. With Tucker facing a defense that has been tough on WR1s, Bowers is the likeliest volume outlet. He's also Cousins' most productive target.

keyMatchups.title: Jets pass rush vs sack avoidance
keyMatchups.body: New York gets sacks at the league's 5th-best rate, while Cousins rarely lets pressure become a sack. Losing Ossai thins the Jets' edge rotation. If Cousins keeps the sacks to one or two, the drive-extending math favors him.

keyMatchups.title: Run wall forces the ball to the air
keyMatchups.body: The Jets' strong run defense meets a Raiders ground game ranked 31st. That leaves Cousins carrying the offense against a pass defense that ranks 25th in EPA. Expect another high-attempt game even without a trailing script.

nextGame.watch: Whether his intermediate throws over the middle come back on target after two straight games with CPOE around -8 to -10.

restOfSeason.body:
The structure behind his numbers should hold. Las Vegas can't run, its defense can't get stops against short passes, and its best players are pass catchers. So Cousins should keep throwing close to 40 times a game, and his sack avoidance will keep that volume efficient. Expect yardage in the 255-295 range most weeks, with his deep-ball efficiency cooling toward a more normal, still positive level as the sample grows.

What regresses is the scoring. His touchdown rate and red-zone finishing are running well ahead of his underlying success. Meanwhile his interception rate is low for a passer with a two-year accuracy decline and four picks in the intermediate range, and it should rise. A realistic finish is closer to 1.6-2.0 touchdowns and 0.7-0.9 interceptions a game: a productive volume passer with a few ugly games along the way.
swingFactors: Whether the Weeks 6-7 accuracy drop is a blip or age
Run game or defense improving and cutting his pass volume

confidence.note: Seven starts with a stable role and volume, but the deep-ball and red-zone samples are small and his accuracy is moving.
